objective: Prove a closed-loop source-variant rewrite search: enumerate structural transform plans from a baseline block descriptor, build every plan from generated sources, gate each on full CPU-oracle equivalence, and rank by measured speedup.

intermediate_gate_2026_07_03.finding: superior variant: the search found replicate8 (8.11x) well above the hand-tuned mlp4 form (4.60x) — a structurally different, better plan discovered by measurement, differences far beyond noise
intermediate_gate_2026_07_03.oracle: mismatch_count 0 on every sample of every plan

falsification_gate_2026_07_03.strict_gate_outcome: failed (recorded honestly; not retried to force green)
falsification_gate_2026_07_03.substantive_finding: The WIN is rediscovered in every run: from the empty baseline plan (2.6-3.5x) the search reaches the 7-9x replication plateau with zero oracle mismatches across all runs and all plans. However, replication factors n in {3,4,6,8} are statistically indistinguishable at this scale: per-batch compute is ~3.5 ms CPU / ~0.4 ms GPU wall, so the speedup metric is dominated by co-load variance (see the CPU-batch trial decomposition). The hand-tuned choice n=4 is one point on a plateau, not a unique optimum; exact-argmax rediscovery is an ill-posed target under these measurement conditions.
falsification_gate_2026_07_03.gate_semantics_history: v1 value-band vs frozen constant (metric-skew failure, true positive); v2 value-band vs same-run reference (self-comparison noise tautology, 6.00 vs 8.79 for the same binary); v3 structure-identity of the top plan (strict; fails when the plateau reorders under noise). The strict v3 gate is kept in code; this record documents why its failure is a plateau finding rather than a search failure.
falsification_gate_2026_07_03.oracle: mismatch_count 0 on every sample of every plan in all three runs

cpu_batch_decomposition_context: A concurrent CPU-batch trial on the same replicate=4 block (i7-14700F, 28 threads) measured: in-process batch compute scales near-linearly (13.3x at P=16, 83% efficiency), and the idealized zero-overhead 16-way CPU batch (0.270 ms) is ~1.5x FASTER than the GPU wall (0.399 ms) at this problem size — i.e. for this block at N=1024 the measured GPU speedup over serial CPU is explained by batch-parallel structure, not GPU hardware. Practical CPU vehicles (process spawn ~15-19 ms, per-thread Vsim construction ~10 ms) failed to capture it, so the GPU's realized advantage stands. This confirms the two-layer boundary: batch-friendly-but-CPU-sufficient (this block class) vs genuinely GPU-favorable (high arithmetic density x large N, NVDLA hot-SS class).
non_claims: no claim that n=4 is uniquely optimal for attention replication (measured as a plateau point)
no universal thresholds; all speedups are environment-scoped measured decisions under documented co-load
PackInputs transform is emit-only and excluded from measured enumerations
